carousels.hook: Google Ads treats a 3-second bounce like a buyer—here’s how to stop it
carousels.throughline: Google Ads charges the same price for a bounce and a buyer, but one setting stops you paying for the bounces.

reel_beats.hook: You are paying Google for visitors who leave in 3 seconds

body.text: Google Ads bills you the same for a bounce and a buyer—even if the visitor leaves in 3 seconds.
Most accounts waste 30% of their budget on these bounces, because the platform doesn’t care who stays.
Exclude high-bounce devices with a -100% bid adjustment, and you stop paying for them entirely.
One account cut their cost per lead from €45 to €12 just by stopping mobile bounces—that’s real money back.

carousels.hook: Meta buries ads that take 5 seconds to show the problem
carousels.throughline: Meta Ads reward creatives that show the problem in the first 2 seconds, not the solution—and 6-second ads convert better than 15-second ones.

reel_beats.hook: Meta buries your ad if it takes 5 seconds to show the problem

body.text: Meta’s algorithm watches the first 2 seconds to see if the viewer relates to the problem—not the solution.
Ads that show the problem in the first 2 seconds get 30% more clicks than ones that start with the solution.
The best creative length is 6 seconds—long enough to show the problem, short enough to keep attention.
One account saw cost per lead drop from €22 to €8 after switching to 6-second problem-first ads—that’s real money saved.
